data.narrative:
Oxide Computer Company, a Series C-stage semiconductor design firm founded by Steve Tuck and Bryan Cantrill, has raised $389M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public semiconductor names (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers in chips and semiconductors, including stage-adjacent companies like Tenstorrent ($2.7B, Series D), Positron AI ($1.0B, Series B), and DEEPX ($529M, Series C).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $389M capital raised proxy, yielding $661M. Peer-median anchoring across the 3 same-sector private comparables—spanning $529M to $2.7B—settles at $1.0B. Public-comp P/S anchoring (median 18.4x across the 3 public tickers) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

The two-method triangulation yields a median valuation of $831M with a low bound of $562M and high bound of $1.1B. Key uncertainties include the capital efficiency embedded in the $389M raised (cash burn rate and runway remain opaque) and comparability of DEEPX and Tenstorrent as stage-adjacent benchmarks given heterogeneous business models within semiconductor design. Revenue visibility and path to profitability would narrow this range materially.
